questions: Can multi-select Dropdown pills be reordered?
How do I enable draggable pills on Dropdown?
Does pill reorder preserve form submission order?
faqs.answer: Opt in with enablePillReorder (Rails: enable_pill_reorder) on multi-select or multi-select + autocomplete. showPillIndex / show_pill_index numbers the pills. By default the whole pill is draggable with an in-pill grip; externalDragHandle / external_drag_handle requires an external grip. Focused pills reorder with ArrowLeft / ArrowRight. React onChange and Rails hidden inputs keep the new order; Rails also emits pb:dropdown:reordered (and pb:dropdown:selected) with the reordered array. Single-select is unaffected; reordering is off by default.

questions: How do I create new Dropdown options?
faqs.answer: Enable allowOptionCreation (Rails: allow_option_creation). The default trigger enables autocomplete. Custom Rails subcomponents must supply an autocomplete trigger or search bar. Creation supports single and multiple selections, including async, and is ignored for quickpick. A selectable Create row yields { id: text, label: text, value: text, __isNew__: true } through normal React selection callbacks, Rails pb:dropdown:selected events, and native form submission. Text is trimmed and blank or case-insensitive existing/selected labels, values and IDs are rejected. Exact ID or value matches keep the existing option selectable even if its label does not contain the query. Pending async searches and errors suppress creation. Creation only selects local text; the application owns persistence.

questions: Does dropdown_field scope country to user[country]?
Does multi_select submit separate array values?
faqs.answer: Pass the attribute (e.g. :country) so the builder can auto-bind default_value and errors from the model; pass user[country] explicitly when you need that nested parameter name instead. multi_select adds [] only if absent, preserves selection order and removes the original CSS-hidden input name while per-selection hidden inputs submit. When selection is empty, the original name and required state are restored, including after Turbo reconnects. These submission fixes apply whether or not allow_option_creation is enabled.

questions: Can dropdown_field yield a custom trigger?
Can I pass a block to the dropdown builder?

questions: How do I change dropdown options based on another field?
How do I replace dropdown options from a Turbo or custom event?
faqs.answer: Pass options_by_context keyed by the other field value together with context_selector naming that element id; the kit swaps options on its change event and clears the selection unless clear_on_context_change is false. To push options from JavaScript, dispatch pb:dropdown:updateOptions with detail { dropdownId, options } or list your own event names in options_event_type. No request is made for you; supply every context upfront or provide the options in the event.

questions: How do I load Rails Dropdown options as the user types?
faqs.answer: Enable async with autocomplete or searchbar. Clicking inside an async Dropdown opens the menu. With no results yet, it shows the empty message (no_options_text, default "No results found") until the debounced search starts and replaces it with loading, results, or an error. The bubbling pb:dropdown:search event exposes searchingFor, setResults(options), and setError(). The kit debounces searches (search_debounce_timeout defaults to 250ms), requires search_term_minimum_length characters (default 3), and manages loading, empty results, errors and stale callbacks. Loaded results stay in place until that debounced search starts. Escape, Tab, or an outside click during the debounce keeps those results; dismissing an in-flight request restores them and ignores the late response. Opening the menu again searches for the query still in the input. Consumers fetch and map standard option objects or rich { option, content } entries, where content is an Element or DocumentFragment cloned into the option wrapper and option retains serializable selection data. Results bypass local label filtering while a search is in progress. When a search returns nothing, earlier results whose labels contain the query stay visible, including text typed after a space. After a single-select autocomplete selection, the input shows the selected label, and opening the menu again shows only retained results whose labels contain that text. A default_value is marked on a later result row with the same id, so opening the menu again narrows to labels that contain that default label. A multi-select selection clears the query and the loaded results, so opening the menu again shows the empty message until the next search. The typed query is not submitted by the Dropdown selected-id input. Keep a separate application field when free text must be submitted.

questions: Does async Dropdown preserve custom selection fields?
Can an async Dropdown have a default before options load?
faqs.answer: pb:dropdown:selected emits the complete serializable option object (an array for multi_select, null or [] when cleared), preserving custom fields and numeric IDs. Form input values are strings. Selected data is retained when remote results change; matching multi-select options remain hidden even if new result metadata differs. Options match on id, then value. Options with neither match the full payload, so two choices that only have a label stay distinct. Pass an explicit default_value option object or array with id and label to initialize async selection with options: []. The builder cannot infer that payload from an unmatched model ID.

questions: How do I submit free text from an async Dropdown?
What happens when an async Dropdown is cleared or reset?
faqs.answer: Async Dropdown emits pb:dropdown:input immediately with { value, reason }, where reason is input, clear, or reset. Use input plus pb:dropdown:selected to synchronize application-owned text and ID fields. Emptying single-select autocomplete clears its selection; emptying a search bar or multi-select query preserves selection. Nonempty edits retain the selected value. Public clear and native form reset clear query, selection, remote results and pending callbacks, close the menu, and notify consumers. Native reset runs after browser controls reset and honors preventDefault; it clears rather than restores default_value. Synchronous Dropdowns retain their existing filtering, selection notifications and reset timing.

questions: How do I observe React Dropdown input changes?
How do I reset React Dropdown?
Does cacheOptions remember an empty search?
faqs.answer: Use onInputChange(text, { reason }) for input and clear notifications. Selection itself does not emit an input notification; use onSelect. In async mode, emptying single-select autocomplete proposes an empty selection even without onInputChange; emptying a multi-select or search-bar query preserves selection. With loadOptions, an empty query and a multi-select selection restore the defaultOptions results. A single-select autocomplete selection keeps that search result list and shows the selected label in the input; opening the menu again shows only results whose labels contain that text. Typing a character replaces the query only while the input still shows that label, including when a controlled value later arrives as null. Once the text has changed, further characters edit the query in place. Backspace and Delete remove one character and keep the selection until the query is empty. Escape, an outside click, or disabling the kit cancels an in-flight loadOptions request and ignores its late response. If that search had cleared the list, the last settled options return, or defaultOptions when nothing has settled yet. Opening the menu again searches for the query still in the input; ref.clearSelected() drops that retry. A search that already settled as an error or with no results keeps that message when the menu closes, and opening it again does not search again. Opening an async Dropdown with no source options, or a search that settles empty and has no earlier label matches, shows the empty message (noOptionsText, default "No results found"). When a search returns nothing, earlier results whose labels contain the query stay visible, including text typed after a space. cacheOptions stores the server response for that exact query, including an empty array. Each Dropdown keeps at most 100 queries. Errors are not cached. Repeating the query after a clear shows that cached response, so an empty search stays empty. Already-selected rows are hidden and do not count as an empty search, so a successful result list or an idle list that still contains options does not show that message when every remaining row is selected. blankSelection is not a search result: an empty async list shows the empty message instead of the blank row, and the blank row is included when results are present. Async options are identified by value, then id, then label. Reset controlled value through the application or form library, or call ref.clearSelected() for an uncontrolled selection. With enableFormSupport: true, native form reset restores defaultValue, clears the query and validation state, closes the menu, and reports the reset through selection callbacks. Controlled parents must accept the new value. Canceled resets preserve state. For application-managed fetching, use async with options and loading without loadOptions; the application owns debounce, query thresholds, errors and stale-response protection. When the menu is open, a new result list focuses the first match so Enter selects it, for both loadOptions and application-managed options. ArrowDown and ArrowUp still move through that list.

questions: Can I use Dropdown with react-hook-form?
Does the React Dropdown submit a value?
faqs.answer: Use a controlled form-library adapter with name, value, and onChange. It accepts name and onChange, and calls onChange with { target: { name, value } } in addition to any onSelect. value is the selected option object, an array for multiSelect and null or [] when cleared, so read value.value in form state. The ref resolves to the kit imperative handle, not an input. With enableFormSupport: true and name, native forms submit selected id (falling back to value) through hidden inputs; multiSelect emits one input per selection and adds [] only if absent. Disabled fields are omitted. enableFormSupport defaults to false, so name alone adds no native inputs or reset handling. With form support enabled, required validates the selection and validationMessage sets the inline required message. Native reset restores defaultValue through the normal callbacks; controlled parents must update value.

PbFormValidation finds the field kit via a *_kit classname, or via data-pb-dropdown / data-pb-multi-level-select for those kits. Server/model validation remains the host application responsibility. Most builder fields also map record.errors into props.error unless the caller sets error explicitly (including nil).
builder.lifecycle: pb_form_with invokes formHelper when available. PbFormValidation is registered with PbKitRegistry; its MutationObserver handles dynamically added forms, including Turbo navigation. Load the Playbook Rails bundle in the host.
builder.simpleForm: No Simple Form adapter is declared by this contract. These methods belong to Playbook::Forms::Builder.

htmlOptions.description: This method accepts props only, not arbitrary HTML keyword arguments.

block.description: This builder method does not forward a caller block to the kit.

submission.value: JavaScript renders one hidden input per selected item id, named name[]. This also applies to variant: single.
submission.multi: Pass user[regions], without [], to submit user[regions][] entries.

validation.required: props.required is used by the kit. The search input is required when empty; kit JS removes required from the search input once currentSelected() is non-empty. Hidden selected-value inputs also receive required, but type=hidden is not constraint-validated.

error.example: Omit props.error, or pass an explicit message / nil to override
error.description: Unless props.error is set (including explicit nil), the builder sets it from record.errors.full_messages_for(attribute).first when present.

validation.client: props.validation_message becomes data-message on the search input. Kit JS clears custom validity when the selection changes.

questions: Can I use this kit in a Rails form?
How do I use pb_form_with or form_with?
faqs.answer: Use Playbook-owned pb_form_with, or form_with with builder: Playbook::Forms::Builder. See the listed methods and examples for this kit. Builder arguments are a separate API from standalone kit props.

questions: How do I show ActiveRecord errors?
Does required_indicator validate?
How do I enable client validation?
How do I set a custom required-field message?
faqs.answer: Most builder fields auto-map record.errors.full_messages_for(attribute) into props.error unless error is set explicitly (including nil to opt out). Checkbox still needs an explicit boolean error flag, and StarRating has no error prop. A required indicator is visual only. pb_form_with validate: true enables Playbook client validation; it does not run model validations. Custom required messages use props.validation.message on text-style fields (including text_area and telephone_field) and props.validation_message on selection-style fields (select, dropdown_field, check_box, phone_number_field, star_rating_field, multi_level_select, and similar). Phone kits own their UI and use validation_message for the empty required copy only.

questions: How does the value POST?
Are names model scoped?
Does the builder read the model value?
faqs.answer: Check the method binding and submission fields. With a bound model, most fields auto-populate values (default_date, default_value, selected_ids, default_options, etc.) unless those props are set. Rails-helper wrappers use model-scoped names; direct kit wrappers assign the name argument to props.name verbatim—pass the attribute for auto-bind, or a nested string like user[country] when you need that parameter shape.

questions: Where do name id required maxlength min step autocomplete and data attributes go?
What can I put in input_options?
faqs.answer: Use the method htmlOptions contract. Text field wrappers accept HTML keyword arguments outside props; select wrappers accept positional html_options. Direct wrappers generally accept only props. Text field wrappers and check_box also merge props.input_options into the Rails-generated field; other methods do not.

questions: Does pb_form_with initialize after Turbo navigation?
Do I need a Stimulus controller to initialize the form?
faqs.answer: pb_form_with invokes formHelper when available, and Playbook registers PbFormValidation with PbKitRegistry for dynamically added forms. This requires the Playbook Rails bundle. No host-specific Stimulus controller is part of this contract.

questions: Can I use these methods with Simple Form?
faqs.answer: The documented methods belong to Playbook::Forms::Builder. This metadata does not declare a Simple Form adapter; host integrations must be documented separately.

block.description: This builder method does not forward a caller block to the kit.

methods.name: typeahead

binding.name: The name argument is assigned directly to props.name. Pass the model attribute (e.g. :country) so auto-bound values and errors can read @object; supply user[country] explicitly when you need a nested parameter name instead.
binding.value: Unless props.default_options is set, the builder auto-binds only when the model attribute is already option-shaped ({label,value} or an array of those). A bare id still needs explicit default_options.

htmlOptions.description: The positional _options and _html_options are ignored. input_options.id defaults to name_input. Other input_options behavior depends on the native/React rendering branch.

block.description: This builder method does not forward a caller block to the kit.

submission.value: Depends on the rendering branch. Native Rails renders a named search text_input; the React-backed branch delegates selection submission to Typeahead.

multi.description: No uniform array serialization contract is declared here across both rendering branches.

validation.required: props.required is handled by the kit rendering branch.

error.example: Omit props.error, or pass an explicit message / nil to override
error.description: Auto-mapped or explicit error is set on props. The React-backed branch receives it; the native Rails template does not forward error to its nested text_input.

validation.client: props.validation.message is copied to input_options.data.validation_message; the kit also receives validation.

methods.example:
<%= pb_form_with model: @user do |f| %>
  <%= f.typeahead :country, props: { label: "Country", is_multi: false, options: [{ label: "Canada", value: "ca" }], required: true } %>
<% end %>
